remove: - **Webhooks are authenticated by their own secret (#479).** `secret_name` is required; it names a vault entry (`talon secrets set support-incoming-webhook "$(openssl rand -hex 24)"`), and the sender presents that value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>`. The value must be at least 32 bytes (serve refuses to start otherwise): the route has no per-webhook rate limit, so the secret's length is what makes online guessing infeasible — use the mint above, never a chosen password. No other credential opens a webhook: agent keys and the admin key get `401 unauthorized`, and there is no dev-open rule. A denied request is never parsed, never runs, and writes no evidence. The body is read whole, bounded at 512 KiB, and must be exactly one JSON value (trailing data is `400`). Zendesk ("Bearer token" webhook authentication) and Freshdesk (custom `Authorization` header on the trigger-webhook action) can send this directly; senders that only sign the body (GitHub, Slack) are not supported — see the [authentication matrix](authentication-and-key-scopes.md).

remove: **Hot vs restart-required.** Hot-reloadable: agent file contents (`enabled`, identity metadata, key binding *name*, policy overrides) and `agents_dir` membership. Restart-required: the company action policy (`gateway.organization_policy.constraints.forbidden_tools` / `.action_approvals`, #425 — loaded once at start and frozen into every generation; a restart activates the change as a new effective generation and invalidates approvals established under the old one), trigger/webhook **definitions** and webhook secret values (#297, #479 — dispatch still re-resolves the current generation, so `enabled` and policy edits govern the next firing), `gateway:` block (organization policy, providers, mode), listeners/ports, scanner infrastructure, pricing and sovereignty. **Key rotation** via `talon secrets set` alone is not detected (the file digest is unchanged) — rotate = set the secret + restart, or touch the agent file. **Secret deletion/revocation of an *enabled* agent is likewise NOT a hot revocation:** the reload cannot build a valid registry for that agent, so the whole generation is rejected and last-known-good keeps the old key serving. To revoke access, **disable** the agent — that IS hot: the disabled generation activates with the prior key carried forward as a *denial-only* identity (the gateway returns an attributed 403; the tenant-API surface rejects it), so the old credential authorizes nothing — or restart.
insert: **Hot vs restart-required.** Hot-reloadable: agent file contents (`enabled`, identity metadata, key binding *name*, policy overrides) and `agents_dir` membership. Restart-required: the company action policy (`gateway.organization_policy.constraints.forbidden_tools` / `.action_approvals`, #425 — loaded once at start and frozen into every generation; a restart activates the change as a new effective generation and invalidates approvals established under the old one), trigger/webhook **definitions** and webhook secret values (#297, #479 — dispatch still re-resolves the current generation, so `enabled` and policy edits govern the next firing), `gateway:` block (organization policy, providers), listeners/ports, scanner infrastructure, pricing and sovereignty. **Key rotation** via `talon secrets set` alone is not detected (the file digest is unchanged) — rotate = set the secret + restart, or touch the agent file. **Secret deletion/revocation of an *enabled* agent is likewise NOT a hot revocation:** the reload cannot build a valid registry for that agent, so the whole generation is rejected and last-known-good keeps the old key serving. To revoke access, **disable** the agent — that IS hot: the disabled generation activates with the prior key carried forward as a *denial-only* identity (the gateway returns an attributed 403; the tenant-API surface rejects it), so the old credential authorizes nothing — or restart.

## Compatibility for v1.17.0

Find your stack before installing. Support describes a product boundary; verification describes evidence for a specific environment. **Supported route** does not mean every client or deployment is certified. **Release verified** below means the named scenario passed against a distributed artifact, not a real paid provider or an entire framework. **Documented / not independently verified here** means a guide exists but this inventory makes no exact-version test claim. **Experimental** is limited qualification; **unsupported** is outside the released contract. Unknown combinations require your own pilot.

Release evidence: [v1.17.0 pilot acceptance](https://github.com/dativo-io/talon/actions/runs/45429574176/job/138573998621), [release verification](https://github.com/dativo-io/talon/actions/runs/45429574176/job/138577644428), [limitations](../../LIMITATIONS.md). The pilot used deterministic local model responses and synthetic business data; the optional paid-provider request was not run.

| OpenAI-compatible application, Node SDK 7.59.0 | Supported model gateway route; use-case bearer key | Release verified: two use cases, permitted response, PII denial, independent upstream counts | [Connect an existing app](add-talon-to-existing-app.md); validate actual endpoint, model, request shape and provider credentials |
